A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 17 pages of v3 and 19 pages of v4, including Appendices A–F, provide readable text, equations, tables and figures that support comparison across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original novelty-detection accuracy, delay, false-positive and runtime results on MiniGrid, Atari and DeepMind Control. Appendices A and C contain additional empirical diagnostics and exploration experiments.

after.justification: V4 retains the original benchmark results and appendix diagnostics, including the Fake Goal experiment now displayed in the main text.

M1.justification: The KL-bound detection rule, PP-Mare reconstruction comparison, DreamerV2 components and adaptations to IRIS and Diamond remain unchanged. The revised propositions and added assumptions concern theoretical justification rather than a changed algorithm or training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MiniGrid, Atari and DeepMind Control environments and novelty scenarios. The Fake Goal experiment highlighted in v4 already appears in v3's Appendix C.2; alternative world-model evaluations on Freeway also appear in both.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain RIQN, PP-Mare, the same world-model architecture variants and KLExplored. Moving Table 8 into the main text introduces no new comparator.

E3.justification: Both versions retain the same metrics, shared-policy evaluation, 300-episode description, Appendix E's 50,000-step description, novelty timings and Table 9 training settings. The exact-fit assumptions added in Appendix D are theoretical assumptions, not reported changes to experimental settings.

E4.justification: The reconstruction-threshold comparisons, training-divergence plots, Fake Goal exploration ablation, policy-entropy analysis and anomaly-score trends are retained. Their redistribution between the main text and Appendix C adds no new analysis or evidence.

E5.justification: Episode-count and averaging information remain unchanged. Neither version reports training-seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests, and v4 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The matched result tables and plots retain their numerical results and empirical findings. Table 8 still reports accuracies of 0.49, 0.46, 0.21 and 0.91 for KL, PP-Mare, RIQN and KLExplored; changing .91 to 0.91 is equivalent formatting.

T1.justification: V4 substantially expands Appendix D with zero-KL and correct-model-specification assumptions, a conditional expected-information-gain derivation and an input-corruption formalization. It also revises Proposition 3.2 and its derivation, and corrects Proposition 3.1's rationale from convexity to non-negativity. These substantially revise the theoretical treatment of the central bound.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same claims: novelty detection using world models, no manually tuned threshold for the KL bound, and effective detection with low false-positive rates across the same domains. The new Impact Statement reiterates existing contributions and future applicability.

C2.justification: V4 adds qualifications about possible bound violations without novelty, KL's non-metric properties and latent-space complexity in Section 5 and Appendix D. Appendix B elaborates IRIS's exploration limitation. The Figure 1 explanation also changes the noisy-observation case from blue collapsing to red to blue collapsing to orange; the underlying plot is unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly describes the cited IRIS exploration trick as heavily sampling the up action. This adds technical context without establishing a changed experimental procedure. Model mappings, hardware requirements, hyperparameters and the DreamerV2 code pointer otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds Vincent et al. (2008), connecting Proposition 3.2 and Appendix D to denoising autoencoders and robustness to partial input destruction. The broader related-work discussion and positioning against existing novelty detectors remain stable.

P1.justification: V4 makes localized wording edits, shortens the running title and adds affiliations, acknowledgments and an Impact Statement. Exploration Effects is reproduced in Section 4.3 while remaining in Appendix C.2; Detection Score Trend Over Time moves to Appendix C.3. The overall section structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The Fake Goal illustration moves from appendix Figure 6 to main-text Figure 2, alongside relocated Table 8. The anomaly-score plot moves from main-text Figure 2 to appendix Figure 7. Existing displays are repositioned or resized, and hyperlink styling changes, but the graphics and table structures are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: V4 corrects Proposition 3.1's non-negativity rationale and makes idealized assumptions and possible non-novelty violations explicit, improving precision and qualification. Bringing the existing exploration limitation into the main text also improves visibility. The gain is limited: revised Equation 7 still does not justify moving from a nonnegative KL difference to a difference of at least epsilon, so the expanded theory does not resolve the central proof gap.
